Hands-on with the M5 MacBook Pro: Apple's new chip is a big GPU jump

Published 2026-10-07 18:40 UTC

Apple's new MacBook Pro looks exactly like the old one, so the story is the M5 chip inside. In our early benchmarks the M5's GPU ran about 40 percent faster than the M4 in the same 14-inch chassis, close to Apple's claimed 45 percent, and local AI models generated tokens noticeably faster thanks to the neural accelerators Apple added to each GPU core.

CPU gains are smaller, roughly 12 to 15 percent in multi-core tests. The mini-LED display is brighter outdoors and Thunderbolt 5 is now standard on every configuration, including the base M5 model.

Apple rates the 16-inch MacBook Pro for 24 hours of battery life; we will test that claim in our full review. Prices still start at $1,599 for the 14-inch M5 model, and the laptops ship on October 15.
